notes: A/B junction is origin. Local +x follows A toward D; local +y follows B toward C.
A and B assumed perpendicular. C falls 1.8 m in local +y over its 13 m length.
D modeled as two equal 9 m segments with an outward bend. All angles and bend coordinates are inferred.
0.8 m offsets from A and B are study allowances, not confirmed setbacks or opening rights.
130 degrees is owner-provided; true versus magnetic north unverified. 192 is ignored.

options.title: Road-facing entrance
options.subtitle: Direct arrival from D; shared living looks into the forecourt.
strengths: Shorter connection from road-side forecourt to entry
Grandpa / sister rooms face the open road-side yard
tradeoffs: Direct entry into compact living/dining needs careful furniture placement
Parents / brother rooms depend on the B-side gap for daylight
Private WC/shower against A require planned roof ventilation or ducts

options.title: Garden-facing entrance
options.subtitle: The same room system turns 90 degrees toward the garden beside C.
strengths: Entry and shared living open to the deeper garden yard
Private sanitary rooms move to the D-facing elevation
Approach offers more separation from the road
tradeoffs: Longer arrival path around the house
Parents / brother rooms need openings toward D rather than A
Stair sits near A/B, requiring roof daylight or planned artificial lighting

rooms.label: Balcony
rooms.note: 4.48 m² external balcony, accessed through sister's room. Shown outside the 100 m² footprint; support, weather detailing and setbacks unresolved.
